messages:
mike: heads up — after the eu canary flip we started seeing a spike in 5xxs and a few API timeouts. noticed right after the weight change at ~1764123400.

pagerbot: @sre_oncall paged for incident P1 — high error rate in eu-canary. See alert: https://internal/alerts/INC-4532 :rotating_light:

sre_oncall: oncall here. joining. can someone confirm whether this is route or model?

anya: leaning route — yesterday's stableflip bumped eu-canary traffic to new green. some DNS TTLs might not have propagated; a subset of requests are hitting old edge that doesn't have the new model artifact, returns 502 from proxy. logs show backend connection refused.

leo: adding context — autoscaler pushed a few new hosts with q8-optimized model variant. kube events show ImagePullBackOff on 3 pods in eu-west-1a.

tanvi: solid. so a mixed state: some traffic to new hosts (ok), some to old hosts (502). that explains intermittent errors and partial customer impact.

sre_oncall: plan: 1) cut traffic to canary (set route weight -> 0) 2) trigger kill-switch feature flag for eu region 3) rollback green -> blue if needed. I'll coordinate with infra for the weight cut.

mike: agree. @leo can you run the dns weight revert command and confirm?

leo: running now:
```bash
# revert canary weight
cli infra route set-weight --region eu-west --route canary --weight 0
```

leo: command returned ok, waiting for propagation. Current fetch: `curl -sS -D - https://eu.api.redwood.ai/health | head -n1` shows 200 on 3 of 5 probes, but we still see a couple 502s.

pagerbot: DNS propagation event recorded: route-weight-change by leo @ 1764123498

anya: I'm going to enable the eu kill-switch flag (feature.flags.kill_switch.eu = true) so app-level routing will short-circuit to stable cluster.

sre_oncall: please post the exact flag command.

anya: posting:
```json
# flag toggle (internal flags-service)
{"flag": "kill_switch.eu", "value": true, "actor": "anya", "reason": "mitigate canary 5xx spike"}
```

anya: flag applied. double-checking: requests now routed to stable by service mesh.

tanvi: monitoring dashboards — error rate trending down from 12% -> 2% over last 4m. latency back to baseline.

cs_ella: customer impact update — CS tickets: ~14 customers reported elevated errors; 4 are high-touch enterprise customers. I'm sending templated notice explaining we hit a partial rollout issue and we've mitigated with a rollback.

sre_oncall: good. I'll keep the incident open until metrics stable for 30m and then we can close with postmortem action items. Quick check: any sign of data corruption or user-visible mis-routes?

leo: no data corruption. requests that failed were transient 502s; retries succeeded after re-route. Gateway logs show higher retry count but no dropped payloads.

mike: action items for postmortem: - make DNS weight cut atomic or wait-for-zero-probing - improve preflight to catch ImagePullBackOff on new hosts - flag rollout gating so feature flag can auto-kill if 5xx above threshold.

tanvi: also add canary health-probe that verifies model artifact present on new hosts before shifting traffic.

sre_oncall: acknowledged. I'll write the incident doc after we stabilize. For now we keep eu kill-switch enabled and will not reattempt green flip until we fix the image issue.

mike: +1. Thanks team. keep me posted on the 15m check. :thumbsup:

pagerbot: incident P1 status changed -> mitigation in progress (1764123520)

sre_oncall: 15m check — error rates steady ~1.5%, CPU on new hosts ok, no new ImagePullBackOffs. will transition to monitoring phase and schedule a rollback postmortem.

anya: I'll leave the kill-switch on and file the flag ticket to auto-revert only after a safe re-deploy.

cs_ella: drafted customer notification and scheduled outreach for the 50 impacted accounts.

mike: closing checklist: verify monitoring, schedule postmortem, assign owners. I'm assigning owners: leo -> infra image pipeline, tanvi -> canary health-probes, anya -> flag gating, cs_ella -> customer comms.

sre_oncall: incident will remain open until 1764123750 on stable metrics, then we'll close and file PM.

mike: thanks all.
